title: In-between Transatlantic (Monetary) Disturbances
hypothesis: An ECB rate hike depreciates CAD, cuts oil prices/exports and GDP with little financial tightening (trade/commodity channel); Fed hike tightens Canadian financial conditions (bond yields, mortgage rates, housing, equities) with slower, broader GDP contraction; magnitudes comparable.
data_sources: Fortin-Poulin 2022 Large Canadian Database for Macroeconomic Analysis
Eurostat indicator sts_inpr_m and FRED Euro Area variables
BAMLHE00EHYIOAS ICE BofA Euro High Yield OAS
sample: Canadian macro-financial monthly sample: 5 Canadian variables (CAD/USD vs CAD/EUR exchange rate, Bank of Canada policy rate, CPI, equity price index, monthly GDP index) from Fortin et al. 2022 Large Canadian Database plus IMF-IFS CAD/EUR; 4 U.S. variables (federal funds rate, industrial production, PCE price index, Gilchrist-Zakrajšek Excess Bond Premium) from FRED/Fed; 4 Euro Area variables (ECB main refinancing rate, industrial production, HICP, ICE BofA Euro High Yield OAS) from FRED/Eurostat sts_inpr_m; plus oil/commodity/trade extensions (WTI price, oil GDP/value added, oil production m3, oil/non-oil exports, 7 export categories, 3 bond maturities, mortgage rate, New Housing Price Index, U.S. macro-financial and Canada-U.S./EU trade flows, 5 GDP components). Monthly GDP used for Canada (robustness to industrial production). Identification uses high-frequency monetary surprises around ECB and Fed announcement windows in interest rate and equity prices. Exact observation count, start date and end date not stated; benchmark includes linear trend and COVID dummy March 2020–June 2021; robustness excludes COVID via sample ending February 2020.
method: Construct high-frequency surprises: interest rate futures and equity price changes in tight windows around ECB (blue) and Fed (red) policy announcements (Figure 2).

Identification of pure monetary policy shock via Jarocinski (2022) rotational-angle decomposition: search over rotations of interest-rate/equity surprises that satisfy sign restrictions (contractionary MP raises rates + lowers equities = negative co-movement; information disclosure = positive co-movement). Benchmark uses median admissible rotation. Report ECB and Fed shock series (Figures ECB_Shocks, Fed_Shocks).
Alternative identification for robustness: Poor Man’s Sign Restriction (Jarocinski 2020) classifies negative co-movement as MP shock, positive as information shock.
Identification uncertainty robustness: normalize admissible rotations to 999 angles, draw uniformly, re-estimate VAR and compute IRFs to build bands combining posterior + identification uncertainty.

Bayesian VAR (benchmark): estimate with 3 lags endogenous, exogenous ECB/Fed MP shocks (diffuse priors), linear time trend, COVID dummy March 2020–June 2021. Normal-Wishart prior per Dieppe et al. 2016 Bear: prior mean first own lag 0.8, lambda1=0.1 overall tightness, lambda3=1 lag decay. Lag choice compromise between AIC 4 and BIC 2. Compute IRFs to one-standard-deviation ECB/Fed pure MP shock; report median IRF with 90% posterior credible intervals.

Local projections (Equation 1) complement: y_{t+h}=beta_h Shock_t + sum_{j=1 to J_i=3} phi Shock_{t-j} + sum_{j=1 to J_y=3} delta y_{t-j} + sum controls x_{t-j} (Canadian, 3 lags) + x*_{t-j} (foreign, 3 lags) + gamma1 Trend + gamma2 CovidDummy + error. Lags selected by AIC. Include lagged dependent variables for seasonality and lagged shocks for efficiency. Estimate horizon-by-horizon; 90% confidence intervals with SEs clustered at time level.

Augmented VARs for transmission channels: add one-by-one oil/trade variables (oil GDP value added, oil production m3, non-oil GDP, oil exports, non-oil exports, WTI price; 7 export categories: oil, energy, minerals, metals, industrial equipment, transport goods, consumption goods) and financial price variables (gov bond yields 1-3y, 3-5y, 10+y, 1-year mortgage rate, New Housing Price Index) and U.S. economy variables (U.S. IP, PCE price, EBP, fed funds) plus Canada-U.S./EU exports/imports and 5 GDP components (IP, durables, non-durables, construction, services). Re-estimate IRFs.

Robustness exercises: re-estimate with PMSR, with LP, integrating over 999 rotations, truncating sample to Feb 2020 (pre-COVID), and contrasting pure MP vs information vs standard HFI conflated surprises to show bias.
